title: Botswana Birding With Your Own Group Means Skimmers, Slaty Egrets and a Shot at Pel's Owl
meta_title: Botswana Birding Trips for Clubs: Areas, Seasons, Logistics
meta_description: Botswana birding for clubs: the Okavango, Chobe and Makgadikgadi, best months, group sizes, vehicles and a 10-night route. Plan it with us.
excerpt: Botswana birding for bird clubs and private groups: where the specials are, which months suit you, and how to set up vehicles, rooms and flights.
content:
Botswana birding is at its best on a private group trip that links the Okavango Delta, the Chobe River and the Makgadikgadi Pans. Those three habitats give a club slaty egrets, African skimmers, wattled cranes and Kori bustards in one route, drawn from a national list of 577 species, with the richest days from November to March.

The organiser's problem is not finding birds. It is fitting twelve keen people with telescopes, long lenses and very different target lists into small camps, light aircraft and six-seat vehicles without anyone missing the owl. We plan these trips through our club and society safaris service, and this guide covers where to go, when, how to set up vehicles and rooms, and what drives the cost.

Quick Facts

  • Species recorded: 577 in Botswana, about 500 of them regular
  • Headline specials: Slaty egret, wattled crane, Pel's fishing owl, African skimmer, Kori bustard
  • Best months: November to March for migrants and breeding plumage; May to October for easier travel and big game
  • Core route: Okavango Panhandle or Delta, Chobe Riverfront, Makgadikgadi Pans and Nata
  • Gateways: Maun for the delta, Kasane for Chobe
  • Ideal length: 8 to 12 nights for a club; 14 nights to add the Panhandle and the pans
  • Group size: 6 to 12 birders, split across vehicles of six or seven

Why Does Botswana Suit a Bird Club or Private Group?

Botswana birding stands out because it packs huge wetlands, dry Kalahari scrub and salt pans into one country with very low visitor numbers. A club can move from papyrus channels to open grassland in a single flight, and the private concessions let guides stop, wait and reposition in a way crowded parks rarely allow.

The numbers behind Botswana birding back this up. The Hotel and Tourism Association of Botswana puts the national list at 577 species, of which roughly 500 occur regularly, and notes that BirdLife Botswana has identified 12 Important Bird Areas. Botswana has no true endemics, but it holds about 85 per cent of the world's slaty egrets and the largest population of wattled cranes anywhere, in the Okavango.

The Botswana Tourism Organisation lists the same headline birds that most clubs travel for: the slaty egret, the endangered wattled crane, Pel's fishing owl, the ostrich and the Kori bustard, the heaviest flying bird. Few places let you tick all of those without a single long road transfer.

For a group, the bigger Botswana birding advantage is control. Camps are small, often 8 to 12 tents, so a club of ten can take most of a camp, set its own breakfast times and keep the same guide for several days. That is far easier than mixing a dedicated birding group with honeymooners who want to chase lions.

Which Areas Should a Botswana Birding Trip Cover?

A first Botswana birding trip should cover at least three habitats: the Okavango wetlands, the Chobe River and one dry area such as the Makgadikgadi Pans or the Kalahari. Each adds species the others lack, and together they explain why ten-day lists here are so long.

The Okavango Panhandle

The Okavango Panhandle is the narrow, permanent river section in the north-west, before the water fans out into the delta. Its tall riverine forest and papyrus are the classic places for Pel's fishing owl and white-backed night heron, and slow boat trips along the banks suit a club with telescopes. Many birding groups stay on a houseboat or a riverside lodge here for two or three nights.

The Okavango Delta and Moremi

The Okavango Delta and Moremi Game Reserve combine floodplains, lagoons and mopane woodland. This is the heart of Botswana birding, wattled crane and slaty egret country, with storks, herons, jacanas and raptors on almost every drive. Private concessions such as Khwai add night drives for owls and nightjars. Our 8 day Botswana photography club safari follows this same Moremi and Khwai circuit, and it adapts well for a bird club that also wants mammals.

The Chobe Riverfront

The Chobe Riverfront near Kasane is the easiest high-volume Botswana birding of all. Sandbars hold roosting African skimmers, the banks are lined with kingfishers and bee-eaters, and the river is busy with waders, geese and fish eagles. It also has some of Africa's best elephant viewing, which keeps non-birding partners happy.

Makgadikgadi, Nata and the Kalahari

Nata Bird Sanctuary sits about 15 km from Nata village on the north-eastern edge of Sua Pan. It covers roughly 230 square kilometres, is run by a community trust, and records about 165 species. After good summer rains, large flocks of greater and lesser flamingos gather on the flooded pan. The wider pans and the Kalahari add larks, coursers, sandgrouse, bustards and raptors that you will not see in the delta.

If time is short, drop the Panhandle and the Kalahari and focus on Moremi, Khwai and Chobe. You lose a few specialists but keep the flights simple. Our Okavango Delta vs Chobe comparison explains how the two main areas differ for general wildlife too.

How Does Boat Birding on the Chobe Work for a Group?

Boat birding on the Chobe runs from Kasane in small, flat-bottomed boats, usually for two to three hours in the early morning or late afternoon. A group of ten or twelve fits best in two boats, so each person has a clear view and the boat can nose quietly up to a sandbar.

Boats are the best platform for Botswana birding on the Chobe because the birds are used to them. Skimmers rest on the sandbars between feeding runs and often let a boat drift close, while kingfishers, herons and storks hunt along the reed edges. Low, stable boats suit telescopes and long lenses far better than a game vehicle on a bumpy track.

Ask for a private boat rather than seats on a shared cruise. The large double-deck cruises are fine for elephants at sunset, but they move to a timetable and will not wait twenty minutes for a rail to show itself. A private boat costs more per seat, but for a bird club the difference in quality is huge.

A good Chobe plan has three boat sessions and two drives over two nights. Combine it with a riverside lodge in Kasane and the group can land, drop bags and be on the water the same afternoon.

When Is the Best Time for Botswana Birding?

The best time for Botswana birding is November to March, the summer rainy season, when migrants arrive and resident birds breed in full colour. The Hotel and Tourism Association of Botswana says a skilled guide can find about 100 species on a good winter day and up to 200 on a good summer day.

Summer Botswana birding has real trade-offs. Days are hot, storms build in the afternoon, some tracks become slow and muddy, and a few remote camps run shorter seasons. The Okavango flood is also low at this time, because the water from Angola usually arrives months later. Rates at most camps are lower, which helps a club budget.

The dry season from May to October is the time most people choose for general safaris. Botswana birding is still good then, especially for waterbirds concentrated on shrinking pools and for the flood in the delta, but the migrant list is shorter. For a mixed group of birders and wildlife lovers, the shoulder months of October, November and April are often the best compromise. Our guide to the best time to visit Botswana covers each month for mammals and weather.

SeasonMonthsWhat birders getTrade-offs
Summer (green season)November to MarchMigrants, breeding plumage, flamingos on the pans after good rains, highest day listsHeat, storms, muddy tracks, more insects

Whatever month you pick, northern Botswana carries a malaria risk, highest in the rains. The NHS Fit for Travel page on Botswana usually recommends antimalarial tablets for the north (checked November 2026), so every member should see a travel clinic well before departure.

How Should You Organise Vehicles, Rooms and Flights for a Birding Group?

A birding group should be organised around window seats, small vehicles and one guide per vehicle. In practice that means six or seven birders per open vehicle, a lead birding guide in each, and rooms booked as early as possible because small camps fill fast.

What does a Botswana birding day look like?

A typical Botswana birding day starts with coffee before dawn and a long morning drive or boat trip of four to five hours, with breakfast packed. The middle of the day is for rest, the camp's bird bath and a log call over lunch. The afternoon session runs until dusk, and in private concessions a short night drive can follow for owls and nightjars.

Vehicles and guides

For Botswana birding, ask for vehicles limited to six guests so nobody sits in the middle seat. Brief the guides on the group's targets before day one, and agree in advance how long a vehicle will wait for a bird. A shared target list on paper, kept in each vehicle, stops arguments about whether to go after a raptor or stay with the leopard.

Rooms and single travellers

Bird clubs on a Botswana birding trip often include more single travellers than other groups, and single supplements in Botswana camps can be steep. Ask early whether members are willing to share twin rooms, because that decision changes the budget more than almost anything else. With 12 people, booking most or all of a small camp also gives you more say over meal times.

Light aircraft and luggage

Flights between Maun, the delta camps and Kasane use small aircraft with strict weight limits, usually around 20 kg per person in a soft bag, including camera gear. Telescopes and tripods count, so plan who carries what. A group that books a whole aircraft gains more flexibility on timing and, sometimes, on bags.

For a wider checklist on contracts, deposits and choosing a group leader, see our page on how to organise a group safari.

What Does a 10-Night Group Birding Itinerary Look Like?

A 10-night Botswana birding itinerary for a group usually flies into Maun, spends three nights in a delta or Moremi camp, three in a private concession such as Khwai, two at Nata or the pans, and two on the Chobe before flying out of Kasane. The order can be reversed to suit flights.

NightsAreaFocus for the group
1-3Okavango Delta or MoremiWattled crane, slaty egret, mokoro and boat birding
4-6Khwai private concessionWoodland species, raptors, night drives for owls and nightjars
7-8Nata and Makgadikgadi PansFlamingos and pelicans after rain, larks, coursers, bustards
9-10Chobe Riverfront, KasanePrivate boat trips for skimmers, kingfishers and waders

Serious listers on a Botswana birding route can add three nights on the Okavango Panhandle at the start for Pel's fishing owl. Groups with partners who want more mammals can swap Nata for an extra night in Khwai. Our 7 day Chobe, Moremi and Khwai safari shows how the Chobe, Moremi and Khwai section links up with domestic flights, and it is a sensible base to build a club route on.

The cost of a Botswana birding trip depends mainly on the camp style, the number of flights and how many people share each vehicle and room. Government park fees are charged per person per day in Chobe and Moremi, and concessions have their own fees, so ask for these to be shown as a separate line. Splitting a private guide and vehicle between six people is what keeps Botswana birding within reach for most clubs.

Insider Tips

  • Book camps first: Small camps decide the whole route, so secure rooms 9 to 12 months ahead
  • Private boats: On the Chobe, pay for private boats rather than seats on a shared cruise
  • Brief the guides: Send each guide the target list and agree a waiting rule before day one
  • Weigh the kit: Telescopes, tripods and lenses count toward the light aircraft limit
  • Mix the seasons: October, November and April suit groups of birders and mammal lovers
  • Log every evening: A nightly bird log keeps both vehicles' sightings in one list

Botswana birding also suits clubs that have already birded East Africa. If your members have done group birding in Uganda, the open water and dry-country birds here feel very different, and many of the target species are new. Frequently Asked Questions

How many bird species can a group see on a Botswana birding trip?

A Botswana birding trip that covers water, woodland and dry country gives a group the widest share of the country's 577 recorded species, about 500 of them regular. The Hotel and Tourism Association of Botswana notes that a skilled guide can find around 200 species on a good summer day, and about 100 on a good winter day.

When is the best month for Botswana birding?

The best months for Botswana birding are November to March, when summer migrants from Europe and the rest of Africa arrive, birds are breeding in full colour and day lists run highest. The trade-off is heat, afternoon storms and some sticky roads, so groups that also want classic big-game viewing often choose October or April instead.

Where can you see Pel's fishing owl in Botswana?

Pel's fishing owl in Botswana lives in the tall riverine forest of the northern wetlands, above all along the Okavango Panhandle and in the permanent channels of the delta. It roosts by day in dense fig and ebony trees, so a guide who knows current roost sites, and a group willing to walk quietly, makes the difference.

What group size works best for a Botswana birding tour?

A Botswana birding tour works best with 6 to 12 birders. Most safari vehicles take six or seven guests with a window seat each, and boats and mokoro stations are small, so two vehicles and one lead guide per vehicle keeps everyone on the bird. Larger clubs are usually split into two groups running a day apart.

Do you need malaria tablets for birding in northern Botswana?

Most birders heading to the Okavango, Chobe and the Panhandle are advised to take antimalarial tablets, because the risk there is highest in the rainy months that are also the best for birds. Check the current advice from NHS Fit for Travel or your own travel clinic six to eight weeks before the trip.

Final Thoughts

Botswana birding rewards a group that plans around habitats rather than famous names: wetland, river and dry pan, ideally in the green season. Keep vehicles small, put the Chobe on the water, and book the little camps that make the trip early.
